scope: POSTHOC capacity diagnostic on already-used cosine new16 systems. Each rank reads TRUE TEST MEDIUM to form a q-PCA Euclidean projection, so these are oracle responses, never deployable low-band scores or capacity lower bounds. The sole question is whether increasing linear q-code dimension above the matched speed255 code can close the observed q255 oracle gap; higher ranks explicitly spend more per-environment code and shared basis storage. This uses the same 1024 training q labels as before, same source/PDE/truth, no new systems, no target-response optimization. Rank255 should reproduce the prior true-medium q projection within numerical tolerance. Interpret only within the cosine statistical family.
